problems.title: Add work rates before dividing
problems.question: Worker 1 completes 30% of a job in 6 hours and worker 2 completes 3/4 in 9 hours. How long together for 9/30 of the job?
problems.idea: Convert both performances to fractions per hour.
problems.note: The paper’s header says “Quiz N4,” although the source catalog files this third available Grade 12 paper under Quiz 03. The explanation follows that existing folder placement.

problems.title: Dilution keeps the salt mass fixed
problems.question: Forty kilograms of seawater contain 5% salt. How much pure water makes the concentration 2%?
problems.idea: Only the total mass changes.
steps: The final mass must be 100 kg.
Subtract the original 40 kg to obtain w=60 kg.

problems.title: Exchange equal masses of two alloys
problems.question: Two alloys of different copper concentrations have masses m,n. Equal pieces of mass t are swapped, making their concentrations equal. Find t.
problems.idea: Write the final concentration of each original mass.
formulas: If original fractions are u≠v: u+t(v-u)/m=v+t(u-v)/n.
steps: Rearrange and cancel u-v≠0 to get t(1/m+1/n)=1.
This is positive and smaller than each original mass.

problems.title: A short recurrence calculation
problems.question: x₁=1,xₙ₊₁=2xₙ+1. Find x₃+x₄.
problems.idea: Calculate in sequence.

problems.title: Two reciprocal geometric ratios
problems.question: A geometric progression has (b₁+b₄)/(b₂+b₃)=13/4 and b₃=32. Find b₁.
problems.idea: Cancel the common first term and factor 1+r³.
steps: Since b₁r²=32, the first terms are respectively 2 and 512.

problems.title: Sum a consecutive block of an arithmetic progression
problems.question: The arithmetic progression begins -4,-1. Sum terms 6 through 14 inclusive.
problems.idea: Its common difference is 3.

problems.title: A zero cosine removes a large coefficient
problems.question: Evaluate 2sin(π/6)-2cos²(-π/6)+√37cos(3π/2).
problems.idea: Use standard exact values.

problems.title: A period forced by the tangent poles
problems.question: Find the least positive period of y=2sin2x+tanx.
problems.idea: Both terms repeat after π.
steps: The function’s excluded inputs are π/2+kπ; any period must preserve this pole set, so no smaller positive period can work.

problems.title: One radian in degrees
problems.question: Find the degree measure of an arc whose length equals its radius.
problems.idea: Use arc length s=Rθ in radians.
formulas: θ=s/R=1 radian; radians to degrees multiply by 180/π.

problems.title: Extend a radius through the diagram
problems.question: In the drawing AC=8,AD⊥AC, O is the circumcenter with radius 5, and C,O,D are collinear. Find AD.
problems.idea: The centre lies over the midpoint of chord AC.
steps: Take A=(0,0),C=(8,0),O=(4,3), consistent with the drawing.
The line from C through O rises 3 for a horizontal movement of -4. Extending the same amount reaches x=0,y=6.

problems.title: Angle between two three-dimensional vectors
problems.question: Find the angle between a=(1,1,1),b=(1,-1,1).
problems.idea: Use the dot product.
steps: The angle is the principal arccosine of 1/3.

problems.title: The principal arccosine is nonnegative
problems.question: Evaluate arccos(cos(-π/6)).
problems.idea: Cosine is even and arccos returns an angle in [0,π].
steps: The angle π/6 lies in the principal arccos range.

problems.title: Choose the nearest cosine root
problems.question: Which solution of cosx=1/2 is nearest to 9π/2?
problems.idea: List nearby roots from both branches.
steps: Near 9π/2=4.5π, the nearest root below is 13π/3, at distance π/6.
The next root above is 17π/3, farther away; the previous branch root is 11π/3.

problems.title: Sine positive but tangent negative
problems.question: Find all roots of sinx=1/2 with tanx<0.
problems.idea: A positive sine occurs in quadrants I and II; negative tangent selects II.
steps: Only the second family has negative cosine and therefore negative tangent.

problems.title: Sum numbers with one residue
problems.question: Find the sum of all three-digit natural numbers with remainder 4 on division by 5.
problems.idea: They form an arithmetic progression.

problems.title: A common ratio also relates the sums
problems.question: If a/x=b/y=c/z=4/9, find (x+y+z)/(a+b+c).
problems.idea: Solve each equality for its denominator variable.
steps: Divide by a+b+c when it is nonzero.
problems.answer: 9/4, provided the displayed final quotient is defined.

problems.title: Each person is counted three times
problems.question: Four boys’ three-person totals are 158,146,164,162 lari. Find the total for all four.
problems.idea: Add the four equations.
formulas: Each individual amount appears in exactly three totals.
steps: The sum of the given totals is 630.
Thus three times the four-person total equals 630.

problems.title: Symmetric roots have a prescribed midpoint
problems.question: For which a are the roots of (a+3)x²-2x-a-3=0 symmetric about x=2?
problems.idea: Their average must equal 2.
formulas: For a≠-3, root sum=2/(a+3), so root midpoint=1/(a+3).
steps: The discriminant is 4+4(a+3)²>0, so there are indeed two distinct real roots.
At a=-3 the equation is linear, not a symmetric pair.

problems.title: Two reflections of one point
problems.question: Find the distance between the reflections of A=(-3,4) across the x-axis and y-axis.
problems.idea: Write the two reflected coordinates.

problems.title: Signs identify the least sine
problems.question: Find the least of sin1,sin3,sin5,sin7,sin(π/2), in radians.
problems.idea: Locate the angles by quadrant.
steps: The values sin1,sin3,sin7 are positive, and sin(π/2)=1.

problems.title: Equate two affine functions of sine
problems.question: Find intersection inputs of y=√2-3sinx and y=sinx-√2.
problems.idea: Set the outputs equal.
steps: The two branches are x=π/4+2πk and x=3π/4+2πk.

problems.title: Right-triangle sides in arithmetic progression
problems.question: Integer side lengths of a right triangle form an arithmetic progression. Which listed perimeter 30,24,26,40 is possible?
problems.idea: Write the sides u-d,u,u+d.
steps: The side lengths are 3d,4d,5d. Since the lengths are integers, d is an integer.
The perimeter is 12d. Only 24 in the list is a multiple of 12.

problems.title: A trigonometric lower bound is attained
problems.question: Find the greatest negative solution of 2sinx+cos²(x/2)+2+cosx=0.
problems.idea: Use cos²(x/2)=(1+cosx)/2.
steps: The left side has minimum -√(4²+3²)=-5. Equality requires sinx=-4/5,cosx=-3/5.
The half-angle parameter t=tan(x/2) then satisfies 2(t+2)²=0, so t=-2.
The greatest negative representative is x=2arctan(-2)≈-2.2143; adding 2π makes it positive.

problems.title: The faster closing rate fixes the speed ratio
problems.question: Two cars meet after 8 hours. With their speeds increased by 14% and 15% respectively, they would meet after 7 hours. Which is faster and by what factor?
problems.idea: The new combined speed is 8/7 of the old one.
steps: The two coefficients are 1/350 and 1/140 respectively.
problems.answer: Car I is 2.5 times as fast.

problems.title: Parity of an even and an odd integer
problems.question: K is even and P odd. Which printed assertion is false?
problems.idea: Reduce each expression modulo 2.
steps: P-K-1≡0, so it is even, contradicting the assertion that it is odd.
P+K+1 and P²+K²+1 are even; PK+P is odd.

problems.title: Recognize conjugate radical squares
problems.question: Evaluate √|12√5-29|-√(12√5+29).
problems.idea: Write 29±12√5 as squares.
steps: Its square root is 2√5-3, while the second is 2√5+3.

problems.title: Take the reciprocal of a defined operation
problems.question: For a⊗b=a/(a-b), with a,b>0, which listed comparison is always true?
problems.idea: The operation also requires a≠b.
steps: Since b/a>0, this value is always strictly below 1.
Its comparison with a⊗b itself changes with a,b, so it is not universal.
problems.note: At a=b the operation is undefined; this restriction is missing from the printed definition.

problems.title: Repeated sine-intersection question
problems.question: Find intersection inputs of y=√2-3sinx and y=sinx-√2.
problems.idea: As in Problem 21, equate the two outputs.
steps: Its two branches are π/4 and 3π/4 modulo 2π.
problems.note: This repeats Problem 21 in the source. Both printed occurrences retain separate explanation files.

problems.title: An isosceles tangential trapezoid
problems.question: An isosceles trapezoid circumscribed about a circle has area 242 cm². The larger base subtends 150° at the circle centre. Find the height.
problems.idea: Let the inradius be r; then the height is 2r.
steps: Symmetry splits the 150° angle into two 75° angles. The corresponding upper half-angle is 15°.

problems.title: A circular sector minus a small triangle
problems.question: In the diagram O is centre of a radius-4 circle, A is above O,OD⊥OA,BC∥OD,AB=OB=2. Find the curvilinear region ABC area.
problems.idea: Its curved boundary is arc AC.

problems.title: Repeated trapezoid problem
problems.question: An isosceles trapezoid circumscribed about a circle has area 242 cm²; its larger base subtends 150° at the centre. Find height.
problems.idea: Use the same radius relation as in Problem 29.
problems.note: This is an exact repeat of Problem 29 in the source and is kept as a separate numbered occurrence.

problems.title: Converge the geometric exponent first
problems.question: Solve 2^(-1+cosx-cos²x+cos³x-…)=∛0.25.
problems.idea: The exponent is a geometric series with ratio -cosx.
steps: These solutions satisfy |cosx|<1, so the infinite series does converge.

problems.title: Area beneath an absolute-value tent
problems.question: Find the area of the triangle bounded by y=4-|x| and the x-axis.
problems.idea: Find the vertex and intercepts.
formulas: Vertex=(0,4); zeros at x=±4; triangle area=base·height/2.
steps: The base length is 8 and height 4.

problems.title: A point one third along a tetrahedron median
problems.question: In tetrahedron SABC, SK joins S to centroid K of ABC. M satisfies SM=SK/3. Express BM using BS,BC,BA.
problems.idea: Write both centroid and section vectors from B.

problems.title: Triangle made by two tangents and their chord
problems.question: A radius-R circle is split into arcs in ratio a:b, a<b. Find the triangle area made by tangents at the dividing points and the joining chord.
problems.idea: Use the smaller central angle θ=2πa/(a+b).
formulas: Let u=θ/2. Chord=2Rsin u; tangent-intersection distance from centre=Rsec u.
steps: The chord midpoint is Rcos u from the centre.
Thus the triangle height is R(sec u-cos u)=Rsin²u/cos u.
Multiply half the chord by this height.
problems.note: This assumes the ratio describes the two arcs of the whole circle. If only an unspecified arc is being divided, its total angle is also needed; the same formula in terms of the smaller central angle remains valid.

problems.title: Separate the even and odd terms
problems.question: An infinite convergent geometric progression has even-position sum 12 and odd-position sum 36. Find the progression.
problems.idea: Both subsequences have common ratio r².
steps: Divide the sums to obtain r=1/3.

problems.title: A right angle from a dot product
problems.question: i,j are perpendicular unit vectors. AB=4i+2j,AC=3i+4j. Prove ABC is right and find its area.
problems.idea: Compute BC=AC-AB.
steps: The perpendicular side lengths are |AB|=√20 and |BC|=√5.

problems.title: Tangent lengths cancel the unknown cevian
problems.question: AB=12,BC=5,AC=10. D∈BC with BD:DC=4:9. Incircles of ABD,ACD touch AD at E,F. Find EF.
problems.idea: Use equal tangent lengths from A in each smaller triangle.
steps: Subtract the last formulas so AD cancels.
Both contact points lie on AD, so EF is the absolute difference.

problems.title: Midpoints connect two opposite side vectors
problems.question: In convex ABCD, AB=a,CD=b,EF=c, where E,F are midpoints of AC,BD. Find the angle between lines AB and CD.
problems.idea: The doubled midpoint vector is the sum of two directed side vectors.
formulas: 2EF=AB+CD; 4c²=a²+b²+2abcosφ, where φ is between the directed vectors.
steps: For the conventional acute angle between unoriented lines, use the absolute value of this cosine.
problems.note: If a directed angle between AB and CD is requested instead, omit the absolute value. Perpendicular lines give θ=90°.

problems.title: A discriminant condition and root signs
problems.question: For 0≤a≤π, when does 2x²-2(2cosa-1)x+2cos²a-5cosa+2=0 have distinct real roots? Determine their signs.
problems.idea: Set c=cosa and use Vieta’s formulas.
steps: Distinct real roots require c>1/2, equivalent to 0≤a<π/3.
On this interval 2c-1>0 and c-2<0, so the root product is negative.
Therefore one root is positive and the other negative. At a=π/3 the double root is zero, excluded by distinctness.
problems.answer: 0≤a<π/3; exactly one positive and one negative root.

problems.title: A perfect-square trigonometric equation
problems.question: Solve sin²(2x/5)-10sin(2x/5)sin(x/5)+25=25cos²(x/5).
problems.idea: Move the cosine term left and use 1-cos²u=sin²u.
steps: The factor 2cosu-5 cannot vanish for a real angle.
problems.note: This final equation is unnumbered in the original paper. It is retained as Problem 41 so it is not lost.
